authoredPrompt: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the extension of Green's Theorem to a multiply connected region with one hole. Panel (a): a blob-shaped region R with a hole; the outer boundary C1 is oriented counterclockwise and the inner boundary C2 surrounding the hole is oriented clockwise, illustrating the positive orientation convention for a multiply connected region. Panel (b): the same region with two horizontal cuts introduced, dividing R into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R''; arrows along the cuts show the opposing orientations (right-pointing on one side, left-pointing on the other) which cancel in the sum, while C1 and C2 retain their original orientations. The figure shows how introducing cuts reduces a multiply connected region to simply connected parts, allowing Green's Theorem to be applied to each piece separately and then combined to give the extended result.
authoredInteractions:
- Drag the inner hole boundary C₂ to resize or reposition it, and watch the region R, orientation arrows, and cut in panel (b) update accordingly
- Toggle between panels (a) and (b) to animate the introduction of the cut, showing how it converts the doubly-connected region into two simply-connected sub-regions R' and R''

discrepancies: The outer curve C1 is a smoother, more rounded blob with only a mild left indentation, while the source has a pronounced kidney-bean hook on the left side and a more irregular outline
The inner hole C2 is drawn as a small, fairly round blob; in the source it is a larger, distinctly S-curved/bean-shaped curve whose bulges mirror the outer boundary's lobes

In panel (b) the source shows the cut arrows clearly on both cut lines spanning from C1 to C2; the generated cut arrows only fade in at the very end of the animation and are small, making the opposite-direction cancellation less visually obvious
The source stacks panels (a) and (b) in one image; the generated figure shows only one panel at a time behind a toggle (acceptable per plan, but the default view shows only (a))
evaluation.notes: A strong teaching artifact: the doubly connected region, clockwise C2 orientation, cut cancellation, and R'/R'' split are all conceptually correct, with rich interactions (panel toggle with animated cuts, draggable/resizable hole, size slider); fidelity suffers mainly from the outer blob being too smooth and the hole too small and round compared to the source's distinctive kidney shapes.
action_items: Reshape rOuter to reproduce the source's deep left-side kidney indentation and hooked upper-left lobe, and elongate rInner into a more S-curved bean so the silhouette reads as the source figure at a glance
Make the panel-(b) cut arrows larger and visible earlier in the cut animation so the opposing-direction arrows (which carry the cancellation concept) are unmistakable
Enlarge the hole slightly by default so C2's clockwise arrows and bean shape are as prominent as in the source
